title: Discovering Your Genjokoan Talk 3
speaker: Myoki Raizelah Bayen
summary: The teacher invites the group to explore their own self-awareness by asking themselves "who am I right now?" without attachment or expectation, encouraging them to become intimate with themselves in the present moment. This practice involves letting go of preconceptions and embracing the current state of being, allowing for a deeper understanding of oneself and one's place in the world. By doing so, individuals can experience freedom from conditioned thinking and ego, ultimately revealing their true nature or "Buddha nature."

But actually, there's nothing to attain and there's nothing to get.

I'm not sure how effectively, it was hard to find the words, but there was a feeling I was trying to communicate: that my life was and is perfect just as it is, not because it was flawless or idyllic, but because it's Buddha's life.
We're all living Buddha's life.
My life couldn't be any other way.
The life that we're given is the life we wake up in.
It's perfect as it is.
*Our intentions equally extend to every being in place with the true merit of Buddha's way.
Beings are numberless.
I vow to save them.
Delusions are inexhaustible.
I vow to end them.
Dharma gates are boundless.
I vow to enter them.
Buddha's way is unsurpassable.
I vow to become it.*
Thank you, everybody.
